# Step 2.70 — Save a copy and upload it

## Builder 1 (file format, saving on the tracker, server side of the upload)

**What exists.** `packages/contracts/src/game-copy.ts`: `writeGameCopy` / `readGameCopy` (refusal codes `not-a-copy`, `damaged`, `unknown-version`, `other-league`, `other-game`), the upload's body `GameCopyUpload` (`{ copy: <file text>, takeOver?: { expectedHolderSince } }`), its reply `GameCopyUploadReply` (`uploaded {added, alreadyThere, notTaken}`, `held-by-other {holder, sentAt}`, `refused {code}`) and `gameCopyRefusalStatus`. The file holds league, game, `savedAt` and each command with its ID and protocol version; no account, session or device. The commands hold player IDs, jersey numbers, tap times, and the name typed for a player added at the scorer's table (nothing else about a person). On the tracker: `game-copy-on-device.ts` (pure: what goes in, file name, `suggestsCopy`), `save-copy-parts.tsx` (`SaveCopy` behind More, `SaveCopySuggestion` beside the notices after `offlineLongMs`, five minutes, with plays waiting). Wired in `tracker-opening.tsx` only (the `slots.more` prop and one line in the notices); `tracker-controller.ts` is untouched. Server: `apps/web/src/server/game-copy-upload-endpoint.ts` and the route `POST /api/v1/leagues/{leagueId}/games/{game}/copy` (body up to 4 MB, `jsonBody` takes a limit now). `replyOf` in `scoring-session-endpoint.ts` is exported; `SessionHolder` is exported from the contracts. Messages: `tracker.copy.*` in `packages/site/src/messages/en/tracker.ts`, including the words for every refusal code (`tracker.copy.refused.<code>`). Decisions T-360 to T-364 (pending files), T6 §4 corrected. No new core command or read, so no role-matrix row; the upload runs `openScoringSession`, `takeOverScoring`, `releaseScoringSession`, `readTrackerState` and the door's `applyTrackerCommands`, all `games.score`.

**How the upload works (T-361).** It asks the door first under a session that holds nothing (saves nothing; answers `duplicate` for what the server has). Nothing new: answered at once, the game not touched. Otherwise it opens the game as the tracker does, on a fresh device id of its own; another device holding it is answered `held-by-other`, and the page must ask the takeover question and post again with `takeOver.expectedHolderSince = holder.since`. Then the new commands go in batches under that session, which is released at the end. Final or called off: `reopen-first` (409).

**What passed.** Unit tests: `packages/contracts/src/game-copy.test.ts` (7), `apps/web/src/features/tracker/game-copy-on-device.test.ts` (4), `apps/web/src/server/game-copy-upload-endpoint.test.ts` (8: copy first then tablet late, tablet first then copy, half and half, takeover asked, uploaded twice, not allowed and visitor, final game, wrong game and damaged). The 8 were seen failing first against a stub. `npm run check`, `npm run typecheck`, `packages/site` tests, `tests/pending-decisions.test.mjs`; the tracker, server and contracts folders as the report says.

**What builder 2 builds.**

- The upload page under `apps/web/src/app/[league]/score/` (for instance `[game]/upload/page.tsx`), linked with the address helper (`leagueUrl`, add a page name if needed), never a hand-written `/{league}/` address. Signed in and allowed to score, as the tracker page is (T-258); reads the file in the browser (`<input type="file">`, `file.text()`), posts `{ copy }` with `Content-Type: application/json` to the route, shows `uploaded` counts, asks the takeover question on `held-by-other` (who, when last heard; reuse the tracker's takeover words) and posts again with `takeOver`, and words every refusal with `tracker.copy.refused.<code>`. All other text in message files.
- A way to the page: from "Your games", the tracker's More (beside Save a copy) or both; say which.
- The pinned lists of rule 9: page-step rows in `scripts/check-web-shell.mjs`, the harmful-text test's page route and file field (the copy route is already in its `ANSWERS`, as `[keeper, owner]`; check it answers there, it has POST only), `unreleased-page.test.ts`, `adminPlaceholders` in `nothing-unfinished-test.mjs`, `activity-messages.test.ts` if a read is added.

**What I distrust.** A copy uploaded after another device re-entered the same plays by hand counts them twice (they have new IDs); the takeover question is the only guard. Plays the first device makes after the upload took its game are listed not saved, and "Send these plays" then refuses them `game-moved`, so they are entered again. The download on iPhone Safari is not tried in a browser yet. The probe and the sends are separate transactions: a device taking the game between them makes the rest `notTaken`, never counted twice.

## Independent review (not the builder; fixed nothing)

Attacks run as a throwaway vitest file beside `game-copy-upload-endpoint.test.ts` (deleted), with `openScoringSession` and `releaseScoringSession` wrapped to act in the gaps.

**High.** A play made on the tablet after its copy was saved is lost to the server once an upload took the game: the tablet's next send is refused `session-not-held` (reason `released`, since the upload let go: "This device has left the game"), and "Send these plays" is refused `game-moved`, whether the uploader was the same scorekeeper or the owner. Reproduce: tablet opens, 4 plays copied, a fifth made after; upload with takeover yes; the tablet sends `[p5]` with `notSavedSince: 0` → `game-moved`. The plays are listed not saved, so nothing counts twice, but every play since the save must be entered again by hand, on a screen that says only "Open it again" (builder 1 named it; builder 2's note judged it "sound": it is sound only for plays inside the copy). Cause: `game-moved-since.ts:52` counts the uploaded events as another's (wrong account, or IDs not in the batch, since `dropTaken` removed them). Smallest fix: the tracker keeps its own taken command IDs in the "Send these plays" batch (they answer `duplicate` and join `own`; tried: same scorekeeper then accepted, sequence 5), and `gameMovedSince` treats an event whose ID is in `own` as own whatever account recorded it (needed when the owner uploaded). The browser test never makes a play after the save, so it cannot see this.

**Medium.** If the release at `game-copy-upload-endpoint.ts:232` fails, the route answers 500 though the plays were saved (and `afterwards` never publishes them to watchers); the game stays held by the upload's own device (`copy-upload-…`) until its lease ends, so the tablet is asked the takeover question naming its own scorekeeper. Nothing counted twice: uploading again answered 0 added, 4 already there.

**Low.** (a) A file over 2,000,000 characters (a 100,000-command copy is 3.5 MB) is answered 400 `invalid-input`, which the page words as a general failure (`upload-copy.ts:70`); the form reads any file whole (`file.text()`) with no size check first. (b) The copy holds only the plays still waiting (T-363), not "the game's commands" as the plan line says: it is not a backup of the whole game; the plan wording should follow T-363. (c) The filter at `game-copy-upload-endpoint.ts:197` is caught by one test only ("the tablet first, the copy late"); "uploaded twice" still passes without it.

**Holds.** (1) The tablet sending 3 of 4 plays between the probe and the take (takeover yes): 1 added, 3 already there, then the tablet's late send all `duplicate`, sequence 4; the door checks `takenCommands` under the game's lock. (2) League and person come from the session and address: another league's game ID at this league's address 404; the file's league or game edited → `other-league`/`other-game`; edited to match, its commands become this game's plays by this person, as a tracker post would. The batch is built by the endpoint, so a file cannot set `withoutMercyOrLastMinutes`, `notSavedSince` or `accountId`; inside a command it is `damaged`. (3) Coach, stranger, another league's admin 403 at the POST; visitor 401; scheduler and owner allowed; the same `mayScoreGame` as the door. (4) 100,000 commands, 999,000-deep JSON as the file, 400,000-deep inside a command, `savedAt` as a string: each refused, no crash. The name typed for a player is not shown by the upload page (counts only) and is rendered by React elsewhere (by reading). (5) Final: `game-closed` → 409 before anything is sent; final between take and send is answered by the door's `isPlayable` under the lock → `notTaken`. (6) Broken by hand: skip the "already has" filter → "the tablet first, the copy late" failed; drop the `other-game` check in `game-copy.ts:127` → the contracts test and the endpoint's "copy of another game" failed. The browser test's `step` catches add to `failures`, which exits 1; nothing passes on a timeout.

## Fix round (T-370, T-371)

**High, fixed.** (b) `game-moved-since.ts`: an event whose command ID is in the batch (`own`) is own whoever recorded it; the account check stays for every other event. (a) The tracker sends along its own taps the server took since its base: those answered while it lost the game (`made` ∩ the loaded state's `recent`, in `lost`) and those dropped from the list (`dropTaken`); they answer `duplicate`, join `own`, and are not counted in `saved`. The real cause was the first: the tablet's late batch had its copied plays answered `duplicate` under the lost session, so they never reached the list. "This device has left the game" with plays "Send these plays" can send now says they wait and points to that button (`tracker.releasedKept`, `tracker-notice.ts`; the generic "enter them again" notice is not shown beside it).

**The attacker (two lines).** A device allowed to score that names another's play IDs as its own: those IDs are taken, so they answer `duplicate` and the plays stay as recorded (nothing twice, nothing of theirs dropped); `gameMovedSince` never removes an event. What it gains is its own new plays let in on top, which scoring permission already gives by taking the game over. Test: "a device claiming another's play as its own counts nothing twice and drops nothing of theirs" (a play of theirs it does not name still means `game-moved`).

**`tracker-controller.ts`, exact lines** (for lane 2.242): the `takenOfList` declaration after `let notSavedSince` (~1042-1043); `showNotSaved` clears it (~1078); `dropTaken` pushes the dropped taps (~1096-1098); `lost` pushes `made` ∩ `recent` after `dropTaken` (~1275-1279); `sendNotSaved` puts them first and leaves them out of `saved` (~2367-2368, ~2387-2388, and the clearing at the end). `carryOnTaps` and `hold` are untouched.

**Medium, fixed.** `letGo` in `game-copy-upload-endpoint.ts`: a release that throws is logged (`games.upload_game_copy`, `release-failed`) and left to the lease; the answer is the counts and `afterwards` publishes.

**Low, fixed (two).** The form refuses a file over 3 × `maxGameCopyLength` bytes before reading it and a text over `maxGameCopyLength` after; the server answers a copy too long 413 `{ error: 'too-large' }`, and so does the route for a declared body over 4 MB; the page words any 413 as `tracker.upload.tooLarge`.

**Tests, each seen failing first.** `tracker-controller-send-plays.test.ts` (late play after the save, copy uploaded by the same scorekeeper and by the owner: listed alone, "Send these plays" saves 1, the server has it once); `game-moved-since.test.ts` (another account's records of the device's own IDs looked past; the attacker; the old "does not look past another account's play that carries one of the batch's ids" is replaced, as T-370 decides the opposite); `game-copy-upload-endpoint.test.ts` (failed release; 413); `upload-copy.test.ts` (413); `tracker-notice.test.ts`.

**Left / distrust.** Not done for lack of commands (60): the `game-copy-test.mjs` extension (late play after the save, both uploaders, the left-the-game words) and the runs of `game-copy-test`, `tracker-route-test`, `bad-wifi-test`, `bad-wifi-visitors-test`. The taken taps live only in memory: a reload between the loss and "Send these plays" forgets them and the send is refused `game-moved` as before. More than 50 taken taps fill whole first batches of duplicates, which do not move `sent`, so a later batch may be refused `game-moved`.

## Finishing the fix round (item 1 done; weak spots 1 and 2 still open)

**Browser test, done.** `game-copy-test.mjs` now runs two games, each on a fresh server: the copy uploaded by the same scorekeeper, then by the owner. A plays once more after saving its copy; back online it shows "This device has left the game. 1 play made here is still waiting…" with 1 play listed and "Send these plays"; the send puts it on the server and each of the 5 plays is there once, A shows 6–5, no `game-moved` notice. 30 checks. The same scorekeeper's upload asks "You are scoring this game on another device… Take over scoring from you, on another device?" (checked as such).

**Weak spot 1 (reload), seen in a browser, not fixed.** After a reload A shows the plain "1 play on this device was not saved" notice and "Send these plays", which is refused `game-moved`. Not in the browser test (it would fail); the controller test "is counted once after a reload…" is `it.fails` and passes only while the fault is there. Toward the fix, committed and tested: a queue state `taken` (`queue-storage.ts`; `settle({ taken })` in memory and IndexedDB storage; contract test seen failing first), `TrackerQueue.keepTaken`, and "Your games" no longer counts a taken tap as not saved (`held-games.ts`). The controller side was tried and taken out again, so `tracker-controller.ts` is NOT changed by this part (lane 2.242: nothing to merge here). What the try showed: the rows are stored and still there after the reload, but the batch sent after it held only the 1 listed play, so something after `begin` empties `takenOfList` (not found within the budget). Also, after a reload with nobody holding the game, the device takes it again and `lastHeldSession` becomes the new session (~line 923), so the batch names the new session: it must name the list's own (the session `restoreNotSavedSince` reads).

**Weak spot 2 (over 50), cause found, not fixed.** `own` is only the batch's own IDs (`apply-tracker-commands.ts` ~236), `sent` is written only when a batch moved the sequence (`noteAnswer`), and `seq <= sent` is looked past only for the sender's account. So with 120 taken plays even the first batch of 50 duplicates is refused `game-moved` (the events after `since` exceed `own.size + 20`). Planned fix, for T-372: `gameMovedSince` says how far, in order, the events are explained; a batch of only plays the server already has is answered duplicate even if the game moved (it adds nothing) and writes `sent` up to there; events up to `sent` are looked past whoever recorded them (sound, as `sent` is only written after a passing check); the tracker sends its taken taps in the order made. Controller test "120 plays in the copy" is `it.fails`.

**What passed.** `npm run check`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run format:check`; vitest on `apps/web/src/features/tracker`, `apps/web/src/server`, `packages/core/src/modules/games`: 189 files, 2387 tests. Browser: `game-copy-test` 30, `tracker-route-test` 79, `bad-wifi-test` 18, `bad-wifi-visitors-test` 26, `takeover-question-test` 30, `tracker-offline-test` 17, all passed. No decision file written (T-372 unused).

## Both weak spots fixed (T-372, T-373)

**Over 50 (T-372).** `game-moved-since.ts` has `explainedUpTo`: from `since`, or from `sent` when later (everything up to `sent` was explained when written, so it is looked past whoever recorded it), how far, in order, the events are explained (the batch's own IDs, whoever recorded them; the sender's End or reopen). `apply-tracker-commands.ts`: a batch that does not explain the whole game still writes `sent` up to there (its taken plays answer duplicate, any other `game-moved`); an explained batch writes `sent` even when it only answered duplicates. The tracker sends its taken taps in the server's order (`base.state.recent`): they were collected out of order (the batch on its way when the game was lost came last), and the server explains a batch only in order. Tests: `game-moved-since.test.ts` "takes the 5 new plays of 120…" (seen failing first) and "refuses the 5 new plays of 120 when somebody else recorded one in the middle" (refused before and after); the controller's 120-play `it.fails` is an `it`.

**Reload (T-373), the two causes.** (1) What emptied the taken plays: `keepTaken` stores a tap the device no longer holds at the end with no league or maker, and `inLeague` lists only the account's own rows, so after a reload none came back. `inLeague.settle` now adds league and account to taken taps (`TakenTap` has both, both storages store the tap whole); test in `queue-storage.test.ts`, seen failing first. (2) The send now names `listSession` (set where the list's sequence is set, and from the stored rows after a reload), not `lastHeldSession`. The controller keeps taken taps as `taken` (`dropTaken`, `lost`), reads them back in `restoreNotSavedSince`, and removes them with the list. The reload `it.fails` is an `it`; `game-copy-test.mjs` reloads A before "Send these plays" in the owner's game (31 checks). No `it.fails` left in the lane.

**`tracker-controller.ts`, exact lines (for lane 2.242):** `listSession` and `keepTaken` after `lastHeldSession` (~1046-1052); `restoreNotSavedSince` sets `listSession` and `takenOfList` (~1080-1081, the old `lastHeldSession ??= session` removed); `showNotSaved` empties and forgets the taken taps (~1086-1091); `dropTaken` keeps them as taken (~1109-1115); `lost` sets `listSession` (~1268) and keeps `made` ∩ `recent` (~1285-1287); `sendNotSaved` names `listSession`, sorts (~2380-2389) and forgets the taken at the end (~2421-2423). `carryOnTaps` and `hold` untouched.

**Distrust.** A taken tap older than the state's 300 recent IDs sorts first in its kept order. `sent` is now also written by a refused batch: sound as it never goes past an unexplained event, but it is a new write on that path.

**What passed.** `npm run check`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run format:check`, `tests/pending-decisions.test.mjs` (11); vitest on `apps/web/src/features/tracker`, `apps/web/src/server`, `packages/core/src/modules/games`: 189 files, 2390 tests. Browser: `game-copy-test` 31, `tracker-route-test` 79, `bad-wifi-test` 18, `bad-wifi-visitors-test` 26, `takeover-question-test` 30, `tracker-offline-test` 17.

## Confirming look fixed (T-374; T-375 not built)

**More than 300 plays (T-374).** `lost` keeps every tap of the device the server answered (not only those among the state's 300 recent IDs; never one in `refusedIds`). `sendNotSaved` sends the taken taps and the list in the order they were made (`at`; taps of one millisecond: those the recent IDs do not name first, then by those IDs, then as kept), and sends the whole list again while a pass is refused `game-moved`, at most `sendPasses` (3) passes; plays already there answer duplicate and are counted once. Chosen over a new server read of the command IDs after the list's sequence (no route, read or contract). Tests, seen failing first: `tracker-controller-send-plays.test.ts` with 301 and 600 plays, with and without a reload: the late play once on the server, nothing listed, nothing stored. With one pass the 120, 301 and 600 tests fail (the test clock gives many taps one millisecond), so the passes are tested too.

**`tracker-controller.ts`, exact lines (for lane 2.242):** `sendPasses` (~589-591); `lost` keeps every answered tap (~1285-1289, the `took` set removed); `sendNotSaved` order and passes (~2389-2444). `carryOnTaps`, `hold` and the not-saved offer untouched.

**"Your games" (`held-games.ts:61`).** Test "counts a play the server already took (T-373) as neither waiting nor not saved", seen failing with the line reverted to `rows.length - waiting`.

**Who may score (T-375), NOT built: it needs a migration.** An event records only `seq`, `command_id`, `type`, `payload` (the engine's command, replayed as such: not room for a server mark), `tapped_at` and `account_id`; nothing says how it came in, and the events carry no session. What (b) needs: a migration adding `game_events.recorded_through text null` (check `in ('copy-upload')`), `NewGameEvent.through?` written by `apply-tracker-commands.ts` when the batch is the upload endpoint's (a field the endpoint sets after parsing, as `withoutMercyOrLastMinutes`, never read from the file), `GameEventMark.through` selected by `list-game-events-after.ts` (and the stand-in world), `npm run db:types`; then `explainedUpTo` counts an own-ID event as explained only if `event.accountId` is the sender's or `through === 'copy-upload'`. Tests then: B naming A's IDs refused `game-moved`; the owner's upload still passes here and in `game-copy-test`. Until then the T-370 hole stays as the review left it.

**Distrust.** Listed plays older than the 300 recent IDs that the server has are shown as not saved until the send (at 600: 251 listed, "saved 251"); only a server read could tell the device sooner. Three passes is a bound, not a proof: a kept order far from the server's could need more, and a genuine `game-moved` now costs three passes of requests.

**What passed.** `npm run check`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run format:check`, `tests/pending-decisions.test.mjs` (11); vitest on the tracker folder, `apps/web/src/server`, `packages/core/src/modules/games`: 189 files, 2395 tests. Browser: `game-copy-test` 31, `tracker-route-test` 79, `bad-wifi-test` 18, `bad-wifi-visitors-test` 26, `takeover-question-test` 30, `tracker-offline-test` 17.
